name: java-guide
Use for Java files (`.java`), `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, or Java requests. Java 17+, Spring Boot, Maven/Gradle, enterprise apps; preview features disabled in production.

Prefer records, `final` fields, unmodifiable collections; explicit types, no raw types or unchecked casts; validate inputs at boundaries with `Objects.requireNonNull`; favor composition/interfaces; prefer standard library. Pin dependency versions explicitly (no dynamic versions like `1.+`). Follow [Google Java Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html). `PascalCase` classes, `camelCase` methods/fields, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` constants; lowercase packages (`com.company.project.module`). One top-level class per file (name matches filename). Use `var` for local variables only when the type is obvious from the right side. No wildcard imports (`import java.util.*` is forbidden).

Use `record` for immutable data carriers instead of manual POJOs; sealed classes/interfaces for restricted hierarchies; compact constructors for record validation. Streams for transformations, not side effects. Never call `Optional.get()` -- use `orElseThrow()`, `orElse()`, `map()`, `flatMap()`. Do not use `Optional` as a method parameter or field type (only as a return type). Avoid parallel streams unless measured to be faster (overhead is real). Prefer `toList()` (Java 16+) over `collect(Collectors.toList())`. Always use try-with-resources for `AutoCloseable` types. Never rely on `finalize()` (deprecated and unreliable). Close resources in reverse order of acquisition.

Packages map to bounded contexts; tests mirror source under `src/test/java`; keep `resources/` flat and use `db/migration/` for schema changes. Test classes: `ClassNameTest`; coverage >80% business logic, >60% overall; prefer AssertJ.

mvn clean install
mvn test
mvn verify
mvn dependency:tree
mvn dependency:analyze
mvn spotbugs:check
mvn checkstyle:check
